entries.title: a C# constructor is no longer reported as having no caller when its class is created
entries.summary: `get_dead_code_v2` reported a C# constructor with no caller however often its class was created, because `new Made(...)` recorded no call. It records `Made` now, for plain, generic, qualified and alias-qualified classes. On RestSharp the `no_callers` rows fall from 101 to 73 in the default call, every row that left is a constructor, and no row is newly reported. A target-typed `new()`, `: base(...)` and an attribute still record nothing; the CHANGELOG lists those and the other limits. An existing index is re-parsed on upgrade.

entries.title: a function used only in a constant or a dispatch table is no longer reported as having no caller
entries.summary: `get_dead_code_v2` reported a function with no caller when its only use sat in a constant's initialiser, a class field or a dispatch table, because those lines were left out of the text it reads outside functions. They are read now. On this repository's own source the `no_callers` rows fall from 426 to 375, on zod from 844 to 686 and on RestSharp from 654 to 625; no row is newly reported. The read is text, not calls, so a name in a comment on such a line also counts; the CHANGELOG lists that and the other limits. `get_repo_health` reads this tool, so its dead-code share can fall.

entries.title: the constructor of a class that is created is no longer reported as having no caller
entries.summary: `get_dead_code_v2` reported a Python `__init__` and a JavaScript or TypeScript `constructor` with no caller however often the class was created, because nothing calls a constructor by that word. Creating a class, or a subclass of it, now counts as a call of its constructor. On this repository's own source 29 of 42 such rows are gone, and on zod 9 of 13. Ruby's `initialize` is not covered yet; the CHANGELOG lists that and the other limits. `get_repo_health` reads this tool, so its dead-code share can fall for Python and JS/TS repositories.

entries.title: a watched repo no longer stays stale after a commit, switch or pull
entries.summary: With `watch-all` running, a commit, `git switch` or pull that changed no working-tree file left the index reading `stale`, because the watcher only acted on file events and none arrived. The watcher now checks where HEAD points once a second and, when it has moved, runs the ordinary incremental index, which refreshes the stored commit. The check reads a few small files under `.git` and starts no process; `SECURITY.md` discloses it. Reported by @randyhbh (#1040). Not run on macOS, the reporter's platform; the CHANGELOG lists the limits.
